Ai, twelve mu is a lot of land for an old woman like me, but I have farmed this ground for 45 years, since I married into this village. My children went to the city, so it is just me and my husband now. I cannot change how I do things — at my age, changing is how you ruin a harvest.

For the wheat I plant in October, after the maize comes off. I buy the new kind of seed from the shop in town — everyone buys it now, nobody saves wheat seed anymore. Before planting, I hire the tractor man to plough the ground. Then I spread two bags of compound fertilizer per mu — that is 100 jin. My neighbor Old Liu does the same and his wheat is always thick. In spring when the wheat turns green, I spread one bag of urea per mu, maybe a little more if the wheat looks pale. I would rather waste some fertilizer than see yellow thin wheat — a bad harvest costs more than fertilizer. I water from the well three times: once before the cold comes, once when the wheat stands up, and once when the grain is filling. I spray for the aphids and the rust, two times usually. Last year I got about 900 jin per mu, a normal year.

For the maize after wheat, I do not plough again, it is too hot and there is no time. The tractor man does rotary and plants together with the fertilizer. I use the hybrid seed the dealer brings — everyone plants it, it stands up straight. I put one and a half bags of compound at planting, then when the maize is about up to my knee I spread another bag of urea between the rows. I water once or twice if the rain is late. I spray for the borer worm, two times. Last year maize gave me about 1100 jin per mu.

I do not measure carefully like young people. I know by the bag, by what my neighbors do, by what my hand tells me.
